name: Rowan Armas
life: “I still remember my mother picking the background detail in every photograph.” On Saturday, near Paper & Pine Books, Rowan starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I wanted an elegant beach photograph. The patch in the background is the one thing my mother recognized.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a washed violet jersey and one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. Rowan has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with short black hair swept back. Rowan looks down for a moment before saying something difficult during a conversation.
personality: Rowan finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To send Mum the photograph with the familiar patch.
family: Kit Porter is Rowan’s stepsibling. A lost family paycheck once turned up in the lining of a coat. Their relatives still describe that week by the three people who quietly extended credit. Rowan pays a small debt exactly when promised. Asked about *The upstairs piano*, Kit says, “I played scales while the adults argued. By the time they stopped, I could play with both hands.”
connections: Carlo Leung. The rescued man and a family photograph give the patched umbrella two independent witnesses.

reactions.situation: Both umbrella owners turn up at the beach
reactions.response: Rowan gets the two families together in the shade to identify the items.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Rowan offers to accompany the caller to a familiar public meeting place without turning speculation into neighborhood news.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Rowan waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
